notes.1: Candidates performed well on this question, but orage in 1(c) was not well known.
notes.2: Many candidates scored full marks. For 2(c) , option H was often incorrectly chosen, and a few candidates did not recognise viande/boucher in 2(e) .
notes.3: Most candidates found this question to be accessible, but for 3(d) candidates often incorrectly chose option A . For 3(e) , candidates often confused the meaning of physique in the text. Candidates often answered 3(g) incorrectly, but there was no pattern of wrong answers.
notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text in which Laure wrote about her brother and his wife having a first baby. The text was mostly straightforward, and the vocabulary covered familiar topics. Overall, candidates performed well on this exercise. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but some answers also required a minor manipulation. If candidates choose to lift more than is required to answer questions, they must make any manipulation needed in the extra material, for example replacing je with elle and changing the verb if necessary. Candidates are therefore advised to answer with the minimum number of words. Most candidates answered 4(a) to 4(e) well. For 4(f) , some candidates had difficulty manipulating mon to son when referring to Laure’s brother. For 4(g) , some candidates wrote too much and invalidated their otherwise correct answer with material that was not relevant. For 4(i) , candidates often kept donc from the original text which did not answer the question asked. Some candidates did not use a subject with conjugated verbs.
notes.5: In this question, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from people looking for an excursion on holiday. Candidates had five people and eight descriptions to choose from. Candidates had to process a variety of information and match several requirements whilst eliminating responses that did not fit. The question is aimed at the higher grades, and candidates with a wide range of vocabulary and knowledge of synonyms performed well on this section. Each person’s statement gave quite specific requirements for what they were looking for, such as location, mobility, suitability for children and specific interests. It is important for candidates to note that these details excluded all answers except the correct one. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question and a global understanding of the texts will not be sufficient. For 5(c) , description 2 was often incorrectly chosen but Claire wanted a guided tour of monuments rather than driving by them in a coach, stopping only to take photos. Many candidates chose description 5 for 5(d) , but Jean wanted a 3–4 hour visit rather than a 5–6 hour one.
notes.6: This final exercise about Ludovic, who goes on a work experience at an optician’s, was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions could be answered with a careful lift from the text, the others needed a small manipulation of the text. Very few candidates achieved full marks, and the questions seem to have discriminated appropriately. Some candidates left several answers blank. Although verbs do not necessarily have to be correct to score a mark, the tense usually must be appropriate to the question and a subject usually needs to be supplied with conjugated verbs. For 6(a) , candidates generally wrote too much and invalidated their answers. For 6(b) , 6(c) , 6(d) and 6(h) , some candidates lifted the wrong part of the text. For 6(e) , candidates sometimes omitted the lui in their answer, meaning that it was not clear that the receptionist was offering the coffee to Ludovic. There was often a lack of precision in both answers to 6(f) and candidates could not gain the marks. Responses to 6(g) did not always answer the question asked and, for 6(i) , the tense used was sometimes inappropriate.
